source.author: ov
source.text: Scylla latus dextrum, laevum irrequieta Charybdis infestat: vorat haec raptas revomitque carinas, illa feris atram canibus succingitur alvum, virginis ora gerens, et, si non omnia vates ficta reliquerunt aliquo quoque tempore virgo.
source.text_original: Scylla latus dextrum, laevum irrequieta Charybdis / infestat: vorat haec raptas revomitque carinas, / illa feris atram canibus succingitur alvum, / virginis ora gerens, et, si non omnia vates / ficta reliquerunt aliquo quoque tempore virgo.
source.text_english: On the right side Scylla, on the left restless Charybdis harasses it: this one swallows the ships it has seized and spits them back out, that one, bearing the face of a maiden, has her dark belly girded with savage dogs; and, if the poets have not left all things made up, she was at some time a maiden too.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: Dextrum Scylla latus, laevum implacata Charybdis, Obsidet: si saxa fugimus, incurrimus in profundum: si contortos vortices evitamus, in saxa deferimur.
reuse.text_original: Dextrum Scylla latus, laevum implacata Charybdis, Obsidet: si saxa fugimus, incurrimus in profundum: si contortos vortices evitamus, in saxa deferimur.
reuse.text_english: On the right lies Scylla, on the left implacable Charybdis, besetting us: if we avoid the rocks, we rush into the deep; if we avoid the twisting whirlpools, we are carried onto the rocks.
